company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, also known as Stanford HAI, is a nonprofit university lab founded in 2019 and based in Stanford, California. It describes its work as advancing AI research, education, and policy to improve the human condition, and defines human-centered AI as an approach that prioritizes human needs, values, and well-being throughout the development and deployment of AI systems. Fei-Fei Li and John Etchemendy are named as Denning Co-Directors. The institute says its research spans the whole university and that it was established to support work bridging disciplines, including topics overlooked by traditional academic departments.

Its stated activities include fellowship and grant programs, affinity groups for students, courses for leaders and decision-makers, specialized training for policymakers and civil servants, and work with the K-12 ecosystem, teachers, and students. It publishes the AI Index, which it calls the most comprehensive analysis of AI's trajectory available and which reports a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared institutions are to manage it, along with declining data transparency. The site also references the Joint California Summit on Generative AI, highlighted in Governor Newsom's Executive Order, and quotes Erik Brynjolfsson, director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab and a senior fellow at Stanford HAI, arguing that businesses can gain more from AI used for employee productivity than from replacing workers.

Research items on the site include Clinical Mind AI, described as a Stanford-developed international collaborative platform for clinical reasoning education through AI-simulated patient encounters, credited to Marcos Santiago Rojas Pino and Thomas Caruso. Another item reports that users with limited social networks who seek emotional support from AI companions experience lower well-being, and a third describes Stanford Law School researchers building an AI pipeline to comb through millions of local statutes. No lawsuits, products, or MCP servers are recorded for the institute, and its recorded legal exposure is in California, with a count of 281.
